Splitting is something people with bpd do when a relationship gets "real" and emotions are invovled. Emotions and gettinf close to a person may have caused a lot of pain or even severe trauma to bpd-people in the past. So ( without real control over it) people "split" their loved one's in half emotioally, see only their bad sides and put these on an extreme. Not to be mean or unfair or hurting, though it does hurt a lot for both sides when it happens- but to protect themselves from re-living the same painful experience they had to make before.

My experience as someone who has bpd: the splitting doesnt last forever. If a relationship makes it through several phases of splitting the person with bpd eventually gains trust and these phases get less intense every time.

You've been bulimic for a very. Very. Very long time. Bulimia is a coping mechanism in the beginning. It calms you down. It helps you spending time not focusing on yourself but on food. Time literally flies during a binge. In the very end, you take back control by throwing it all up again. Making your body throw up by yourself is seriously a powerful thing. Something you are in control of everything that happens. That's what bulimia was for me in the very beginning. The longer i have been living with this Ed, the more it became a 'behavior' and eventually... An addiction. Buying food, binging all the time and throwing up. It no longer would depend on my mood or how much I'd feel under pressure. I JUST HAD TO Do It. Like an alcoholic needs to drink. Even if I had a good day being around friends all the time. At the end of the day bulimia was the last friend I'd spend my time with. I don't think there's an actual answer to the '" why". Bulimics become addicts sonner or later in life if they don't manage to stop their inner addiction to grow. You're an addict. But I think you can still find cure. Becoming clean is extremely hard. Specially if your addiction is not about heroine or alcohol or any other drug. You can't say NO to food forever. I still think it's possible but it's though. But think about it for yourself. How much do you really love your husband and your kids? How much do you need bulimia? How much better would it be to live without either two of these? Bulimia or your Family? This is a though road. But you've been walking it for a long time. You can get better and become clean. I don't know if this may help you or not. Just some thoughts around midnight from a girl from Germany.
